Required Dismantle trait implementations for RDF terms, sort keys and compiled arguments forward to the one allocation-free dismantle_tree home; each tree supplies its own typed child traversal and no destruction algorithm is duplicated.

These required provider declarations explicitly attest that selecting first, last or the ownership fixture performs no exact arithmetic. The default refuses opaque bounded cost analysis, so each priced native provider must override it; zero is a declaration, not a second arithmetic implementation.

Typed public explanation and result carriers wrap different payload values through the single payload admission and lease home; the concrete return types preserve public interfaces without a second allocation or lease implementation.

Opposite typed conversions bridge the generic view row and the concrete resident quad row by moving their four fields unchanged. They preserve the public carrier types without an allocation, remapping algorithm or duplicated storage operation.

The immutable and exclusive mutable slice views must have distinct Rust borrow signatures. Both preserve the original caller/native array owner and grant; sharing a mutable accessor with the immutable one would require an invalid exclusive borrow or unsafe aliasing.

Required std::error::Error adapters expose the original native failure carried by two distinct public error enums. All other variants have no nested source; the forwarding match implements each concrete trait contract without copying the failure or its owner.
